title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 136, the divided-power de Rham complex, 1976 IHES lecture). The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript of SGA 7 IX (Grothendieck's exposé on Néron models and semi-stable reduction). This handwritten sheet appears to be written on the back of that typescript, so the neighbouring transcriptions are unrelated to its content.

A_* (written A_α or A_* in the manuscript) is a simplicial graded-commutative divided-power algebra. Its degree-0 part is A_n^0 = Γ{X_0,...,X_n}/(X_0+...+X_n-1), the divided-power (PD) functions on the algebraic n-simplex; presumably A_n is the PD de Rham complex of this simplex. For a monotone map σ: Δ_n → Δ_1 the structure map A(σ): A_1 → A_n is pullback of barycentric coordinates: A(σ)(X_0) = Σ_{σ(j)=0} X_j and A(σ)(X_1) = Σ_{σ(j)=1} X_j. So this is a divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial forms ∇(n,*).

The proposition being proved, as far as can be inferred: an endomorphism (or morphism) φ of A_1 compatible with the two augmentations α, β: A_1 → A_0 (evaluation at the vertices) extends uniquely to a family φ_n on A_n. The family satisfies φ_n∘A(σ) = A(σ)∘φ for every σ: Δ_n → Δ_1, and it is a simplicial morphism.

The top lines check compatibility with composition: φ_n(A(τ)A(σ)) = A(τ)φ_m A(σ) = A(στ)φ, using the hypothesis on φ_m and then on φ_n. Grothendieck marks this 'OK'.

The proof proceeds by cases.
- n = 0 is trivial.
- For n = 1, the maps are σ = id and the two constant maps, and A(constant at 0) = α, A(constant at 1) = β. So the condition is exactly the hypothesis that φ respects the augmentations.
- For n ≥ 2, the non-constant σ are the n surjections σ_r (0 ≤ r ≤ n-1), with σ_r = 0 on {0..r} and 1 on {r+1..n}. They give A(σ_r)(X_0) = X_0+...+X_r =: U_r (partial sums) and A(σ_r)(X_1) = X_{r+1}+...+X_n = 1-U_r. Because the maps are PD-morphisms, one needs A(σ_r)(X_0^{(i)}) = U_r^{(i)}.

The key lemma states that the U_r^{(i)} (i ≥ 1, 0 ≤ r ≤ n-1) generate A_n^0, and that A_n^0 ≅ Γ{U_0,...,U_{n-1}} as a PD-algebra. This is correct: X_0 = U_0, X_r = U_r - U_{r-1}, and X_n = 1 - U_{n-1} is a unimodular change of variables. Divided powers of sums and differences are given by the PD binomial formula, so Γ{X_1..X_n} = Γ{X_0..X_{n-1}} = Γ{U_0..U_{n-1}}. Hence φ_n on A_n^0 is forced on the generators U_r^{(i)}, and it exists because these are free PD generators.

Geometrically, the n surjections embed the PD n-simplex into the n-fold product of PD intervals. So the simplicial PD algebra is 'generated by its 1-simplex' together with the two vertices. This gives a rigidity/universal-property statement for the simplicial PD de Rham algebra, presumably used to compare it with cochains or to construct operations on it.
errors: The transcription of the compatibility lines is garbled; the image reads φ_n(A(τ)A(σ)) = A(τ)φ_m A(σ), with the underbraces A(στ) and A(σ)φ.
The lemma's sentence is cut off at the end of the page ('isomorphe en tant que ... à Γ{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}'). Presumably it continues 'en tant que Γ-algèbre'.

ideas.what: Simplicial algebra of divided-power polynomial (de Rham) forms on algebraic simplices, with structure maps given by pulling back barycentric coordinates
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial cdga ∇(•,*) / A_PL; PD de Rham complex of simplices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) and Cartan's 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976) for polynomial forms; PD versions appear in later integral/p-adic homotopy work (e.g. Cenkl–Porter style constructions)
ideas.where_published: Only as the unpublished 1976 IHES lecture (this cote)

ideas.what: Lemma: the degree-0 part of the PD n-simplex is the free divided-power algebra on the partial sums U_r = X_0+...+X_r, which are pullbacks of the coordinate along the n surjections Δ_n → Δ_1
ideas.modern_name: Free PD algebra under unimodular change of coordinates; the PD simplex embeds in a product of PD intervals

ideas.what: A morphism of the 1-simplex level compatible with the two augmentations extends uniquely to a morphism of the whole simplicial PD algebra
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / generation of the simplicial PD-forms algebra by the interval

missed.claim: This is part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 treatment of an integral (divided-power) version of the simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra. It is contemporaneous with, and independent of, Sullivan and Cartan. The page itself contains only a routine generation lemma.
missed.quote: Lemme Les U_r^{(i)} (i≥1, 0≤r≤n-1) engendrent la algèbre A_n^0, qui est isomorphe ... à Γ{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck pursued PD/integral commutative cochain models in 1975–76. Such models relate to modern integral and p-adic homotopy theory (Mandell, Toën, Horel and others). The mathematical content of this page is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification: free PD generators given by partial sums, used to extend a map from the 1-simplex level. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished PD-de Rham simplicial programme.

The 'A_α' is often closer to 'A_*' in the image.
'σ_r' is preceded by a struck-out symbol; the range note '(0 ≤ r ≤ n-1)' is correct.
The neighbouring 'pages' are SGA 7 exposé IX typescript, which is reused paper (verso) and unrelated to this content.
